items.description: Sec. 4.1 only calls the problem a 'classic 2D cantilever beam'. The later phrase 'fixed-boundary corners' suggests a fixed left edge, but which edge is fixed, and over what length, is shown only in the Fig. 3 problem-setup panel (bottom left). The text never states it.
readings: Entire left edge (x = 0, 0 ≤ y ≤ 100 mm) fixed
Only short segments or nodes at the top-left and bottom-left corners fixed
Only a central segment of the left edge fixed

items.entity: Constraint type on the left-edge support
items.description: For Sec. 4.1 the text says only 'cantilever' and 'fixed-boundary'. It never says which degrees of freedom are restrained. By contrast, Sec. 4.3 explicitly says 'fully clamped' for its own case.
readings: Fully clamped: ux = uy = 0 at every supported node
ux = 0 along the edge with uy = 0 at a single node only (roller-type wall)

items.entity: 100 MPa traction on the right edge
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says to 'apply a 100 MPa traction to the right edge of the beam', which suggests the whole edge. Sec. 4.4 says 'Returning to the purely structural cantilever of Section 4.1, with the traction applied at the center of the right edge', which suggests a central patch. The actual placement appears only in Fig. 3.
readings: Patch centred at mid-height of the right edge (y = 0.5H = 50 mm)
Uniform over the full right edge (y = 0 to 100 mm)
At the bottom-right corner (y = 0), as in the classic 99/88-line cantilever

items.entity: Length of the loaded segment on the right edge
items.description: The load is a traction in MPa, so it must act over a finite edge length. Neither Sec. 4.1 nor Sec. 4.4 ('at the center of the right edge') gives the length of the loaded patch.
readings: One element edge (1 mm) at mid-height, close to a point load
Short central patch of a few elements (about 2–10 mm)
Wider central patch (about 20–30 mm, i.e. 20–30% of the height)
Entire 100 mm right edge

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the magnitude ('100 MPa traction'), not the direction. Sec. 4.3 says 'downward', but that is a different case. In Sec. 4.5 'traction ... applied to the top face' means a load normal to the face, so a normal (axial) reading of Sec. 4.1 is also possible. The arrow appears only in Fig. 3.
readings: Transverse, downward (−y) shear traction
Transverse, upward (+y) shear traction (mirror-image design)
Normal to the edge (axial, +x tension or −x compression)

items.entity: Resultant force of the 100 MPa traction
items.description: A traction of 100 MPa on a plane-stress thickness of 1 mm (Sec. 4) gives 100 N per mm of edge. The total force or nodal-load magnitude therefore depends on the unspecified loaded length. For the elastic-compliance baseline this only scales the compliance value.
readings: 100 N (1 mm patch)
About 1 kN (10 mm patch)
About 2–3 kN (20–30 mm patch)
10 kN (full 100 mm edge)

items.description: The text never says whether any part of the 200×100 mm domain is non-design, for example a solid pad under the loaded patch or a strip along the clamped edge. The setup is drawn only in Fig. 3.
readings: None: the whole 200×100 mm rectangle is designable
Solid non-design pad under the loaded patch on the right edge
Solid non-design strip along the clamped left edge

items.description: No starting design is given for the 2D examples; only the Sec. 4.5 blade is initialised (θ = 0.5). With RAMP q = 8 the problem is non-convex, and Sec. 4.3 itself attributes differences between designs to the non-convex landscape.
readings: Uniform ρ = V* = 0.5
Uniform ρ = 1.0
Random or perturbed field around 0.5

items.entity: Density field used in the volume constraint
items.description: Eq. 19 integrates ρ, the raw design variables. Sec. 3.2, however, says the filtered ρ̃ is the physical density. Because the normalised hat filter does not exactly preserve volume near boundaries, it matters which field is constrained to V* = 0.5.
readings: Constraint applied to raw ρ (Eq. 19 as written)
Constraint applied to filtered ρ̃ (physical density)

items.entity: Objective scaling/normalisation of J_el = f_ext^T u_0 for MMA
items.description: The text gives no scaling or normalisation of the objective passed to MMA. Sec. 4.3 explicitly notes 'MMA sensitivity to objective magnitude', so the scaling can change the converged design.
readings: Unscaled J_el in N·mm (mJ)
J_el divided by its value for the initial design
J_el in J, or another fixed scale factor

items.description: Sec. 3.4 says only that the Deetman MMA implementation was used 'with default parameters'. Sec. 4 fixes the move limit at 0.1 and uses the default asymptote initialisation, but a0, a_i, c_i and d_i are never stated.
readings: Larger c_i (e.g., 1e4)

items.description: Sec. 3.5 says the run stops when 'the design and objective change fall below a prescribed tolerance', but no objective tolerance is given. Sec. 4 says the run stops at 250 iterations or when ||ρ_i − ρ_{i−1}||∞ ≤ 1e-5, with no objective criterion.
readings: Stop at 250 iterations or when max design change ≤ 1e-5 only
Also stop when relative objective change < tolerance (e.g., 1e-4 or 1e-6)

locator: Sec. 4.1, the structural cantilever baseline design minimizing elastic compliance (Fig. 3)
